reAudit2.disclosure: This second re-audit's report text was lost to context compaction before it was written into this artifact and could not be recovered from the session transcript. Its findings are recorded here as they were acted on, not as a verbatim quotation - this is a provenance weakness of THIS artifact, and it is the reason a third audit was commissioned against the final freeze and recorded verbatim below.
findingsAsActedOn: B2' - a quantitative value sitting inside a REVIEW_UNCERTAIN or INFORMATIONAL item's span was credited as covered, although such items account for no text.
A REVIEW_UNCERTAIN item left MISSING_FROM_COMPOSITION did not block semantic completeness - materiality undetermined was effectively treated as immaterial.
An accountability result that was not semanticallyComplete could reach compile with no failure reason when no other accountability reason fired.
A proviso tail after a comma or semicolon was hidden behind a covered main clause because it was not its own segment.
The general 40-character segment floor and the segment vocabulary were too narrow (auditor asked for a 24-char floor and a wider word list).
reAudit2.disposition: First four fixed in commit 8c with 2 new tests. The fifth was ATTEMPTED AND REJECTED ON EVIDENCE: lowering the floor to 24 and widening the vocabulary made colon-terminated lead-ins fire as gaps across eleven synthetic corpus scenarios (I3, I12, I13, I14, I22, I23, I24, I25, I26, I32, I40) plus the agreement rollup test. Calibrating a detector by loosening it until the corpus breaks is not a fix; the floor stayed at 40 and the conditional-tail rule was added instead, which covers the short-proviso case the auditor was protecting without the false positives. Audit 3 finding 4 shows the residual consequence of that decision and is carried as an open defect, not as a settled question.

reAudit3.verbatimReport:
## VERDICT: **BLOCKER**

Material operative text - a whole guarantee-and-lien covenant, an absolute prohibition, enumerated Lien carve-outs, a 30-day cure period, a maturity date, and a $75M cap in an expanded definition - can each be dropped by this pipeline with **zero** surfaced signal: `INVENTORY_OK`, `uninventoriedSegments: []`, `semanticallyComplete: true`, `failureReasons: []`, and an agreement rollup of `SEMANTICALLY_COMPLETE`. Demonstrated by driving the real `runSemanticInventory` / `reconcileInventoryWithComposition` / `rollupAgreementSemanticStatus` with a scripted `StageCaller` (scripts in `/tmp/aud/`).

The layer's fail-safes that were *actually tested by the repo's own suite* (non-covering gap items, a throwing gap call, non-material echo items, the status-string-alone path) all hold. The defects are all in the **entry conditions** to the accounting - what is even *eligible* to be called a gap - which the tests never probe.

---

### 1. BLOCKER - the drafting-vocabulary gate is an unconditional opt-out for whole clauses
`lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-accountability/inventory.ts:119` (`OPERATIVE_SEGMENT_RE`), applied at `:165`.

A segment is only *eligible* to be a gap if it matches that word list. Text that does not is never a gap at any coverage, at any length.

Input (operative region):
```
Section 7.11. The Borrower shall deliver to the Administrative Agent a compliance certificate signed by a Responsible Officer. The Borrower will cause each Subsidiary formed after the Closing Date to become a Guarantor and to grant a first-priority security interest in substantially all of its assets.
```
Model returns ONE item: the compliance-certificate sentence, `MATERIAL`. The second sentence - a springing guarantee **and** an all-assets first-lien grant - is a clean, correctly-split segment at chars 127-302, 148 non-whitespace chars, **0% covered**, and contains none of `shall|may|must|means|agrees|covenants|provided|except|other than|excluding|including|to the extent|unless|subject to|so long as|...`.

Observed:
```
inventoryStatus       : INVENTORY_OK
uninventoriedSegments : 0   []
uninventoriedValues   : 0   []
gapReinventory        : {"attempted":false,...}   <- no gap call was even made
semanticallyComplete  : true       reasons: []
compile failureReasons: []                        -> determineStatus (compile.ts:136-137) = COMPLETED
AGREEMENT ROLLUP      : SEMANTICALLY_COMPLETE
```
Pass C's per-item report contains **one** row (the accepted item). The dropped covenant contributes no row, no count, no reason string anywhere in the frozen record.

Why it matters: `docs/phase3-final-closure/05-architecture-decision.json` claims the mechanism's expected effect is that "*region-tail omissions (a whole trailing definition left uncovered) ... become either inventoried by the gap call or visibly surfaced.*" This is a whole trailing covenant, left uncovered, that is **neither**. Ordinary US credit-agreement drafting uses `will`, `agrees to cause`, `is obligated to`, `undertakes`, `it shall be a condition precedent that` - the list is a closed vocabulary presented as a generic net, and the false-negative side of it is undisclosed. This alone falsifies "can no longer silently omit material operative content."

### 2. BLOCKER - `semanticallyComplete` does **not** require zero uninventoried values
`reconciliation.ts:426` and `:439`:
```ts
const operativeEconomicUninventoried = inventory.uninventoriedValues
  .filter((v) => v.regionId === "operative" && (v.kind === "MONEY" || v.kind === "PERCENT" || v.kind === "RATIO"));
```
`inventory.uninventoriedValues.length` is computed (`inventory.ts:186-191`) and reported in `counts` (`:458`) but is **never** a completeness input. Only 3 of the 9 `QUANTITATIVE_KINDS` in a single hardcoded `regionId` gate anything.

Driving one uncovered value of each kind through the real functions (covered item = an unrelated MATERIAL sentence):

| uncovered value in operative text | `uninventoriedValues` | `semanticallyComplete` | compile failureReasons |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$12,500,000` (MONEY) | 1 | false | `SEMANTIC_ACCOUNTABILITY_INCOMPLETE` |
| `25 basis points` (PERCENT) | 1 | false | `SEMANTIC_ACCOUNTABILITY_INCOMPLETE` |
| `2.00 to 1.00` (RATIO) | 1 | false | `SEMANTIC_ACCOUNTABILITY_INCOMPLETE` |
| **`30 days`** (DAYS) | 1 | **true** | **`[]` SILENT** |
| **`6 months`** (PERIOD) | 1 | **true** | **`[]` SILENT** |
| **`March 31, 2030`** (DATE) | 1 | **true** | **`[]` SILENT** |
| **`1.75 times`** (MULTIPLIER) | 1 | **true** | **`[]` SILENT** |

A dropped cure period, grace period, notice period, availability period, maturity date, or incremental-facility multiple is invisible. The claim under audit ("zero uninventoried values") is false as written, and the narrowing to money/percent/ratio appears nowhere in the Phase 3 closure decision record (`grep` of `docs/phase3-final-closure/` for the money/percent/ratio subset: no hits) - only in a code comment.

### 3. BLOCKER - coverage accounting never runs on expansion regions, and their economic values are exempt too
`inventory.ts:324-325` (segments computed for `kind === "OPERATIVE"` only) plus the `regionId === "operative"` filter at `reconciliation.ts:426`.

Input: operative text `The Borrower shall not make Investments other than Permitted Investments as defined in Section 1.01.` (fully covered by one MATERIAL item), plus a `CROSS_REFERENCE_EXPANSION` region `xref-0`:
```
Permitted Investments means investments not to exceed $75,000,000 in the aggregate; provided that no
Default shall have occurred and the Borrower shall pledge the equity of each such Person.
```
Observed: `INVENTORY_OK`, `uninventoriedSegments: 0`, `uninventoriedValues: 1 ["MONEY:$75,000,000"]`, `semanticallyComplete: **true**`, `failureReasons: []`.

The entire incorporated definition - the cap, the no-Default condition, and the pledge requirement - is unaccounted, and even the `$75,000,000` escapes the money gate purely because of a hardcoded region-id string. Doc 05 discloses that *text* accounting is operative-only ("their own units account for them"); it does **not** disclose that the value gate is region-scoped the same way, and the "their own units account for them" premise does not hold for an inline definition that has no unit of its own.

### 4. MAJOR - the 40-char floor drops substantive clauses, not just "connective noise"
`inventory.ts:115` + `:164-165`.

- `"The Borrower shall not incur Debt."` - 29 non-ws chars, a correctly segmented, 0%-covered absolute prohibition containing `shall`. Result: `INVENTORY_OK / 0 segments / semanticallyComplete true / failureReasons []`.
- Enumerated carve-outs are systematically below the floor. Input `... any Lien upon any of its property, other than the following: (i) Liens for taxes not yet due; (ii) statutory Liens of landlords; (iii) Liens securing Priority Debt; (iv) Liens on Foreign Subsidiary equity.` Segmenter output (verified): the four carve-outs are 26/30/31/35 non-ws chars - **all four below the floor**. One item covering only the lead-in yields `INVENTORY_OK`, `0` segments, `semanticallyComplete: true`, `failureReasons: []`.

Doc 05 discloses the floor but justifies it as excluding *"sub-40-char fragments ('and any other ...')"* that are *"least likely to change a compliance conclusion on their own."* A Lien basket schedule and an absolute debt prohibition falsify that justification. The floor is disclosed; **this consequence is not**.

### 5. MAJOR - an enumerator prefix defeats the conditional-tail lower floor, contradicting the code's own comment
`inventory.ts:116-117` and `:123`. The comment states: *"a missing condition is never normalized away because it is short."* `OPENS_WITH_CONDITIONAL_RE` is anchored `^\s*<connective>`, so any enumerator prefix disqualifies it.

Minimal repro (`findUncoveredOperativeSegments("operative", text, [])`, no accepted spans at all):
```

"The Borrower shall not incur Debt. (iv) except Liens for taxes not yet due."   -> []                                        SILENT
```
Adding `(iv) ` - the normal way exceptions are drafted - converts a surfaced gap into silence.

### 6. MAJOR - coverage arithmetic: up to half of a boundary-free segment vanishes
`inventory.ts:118` (`SEGMENT_COVERED_THRESHOLD = 0.5`) + `:151-160`. Measured cliff on a single segment:
```
span covering 45% -> 1 uncovered segment (coverage 0.452)
span covering 50% -> 0
span covering 51% -> 0
span covering 60% -> 0
```
Concrete: one sentence, no internal boundary punctuation -
```
The Borrower shall cause the Collateral Agent to hold a perfected first priority security interest
in all Collateral at all times and the Borrower shall not permit any Subsidiary to become an obligor
in respect of Indebtedness that is contractually senior in right of payment to the Notes
```
One MATERIAL item covering the first 55% -> `INVENTORY_OK`, `0` segments, `semanticallyComplete: true`, `[]`. The entire structural-subordination covenant is dropped.

Same mechanism with a proviso that the segmenter does not split (`SEGMENT_BOUNDARY_RE`, `:124`, only splits a connective preceded by `,` or `;`):
- `... so long as no Event of Default has occurred ... [covered] and the Borrower has delivered an officer certificate certifying pro forma compliance with the financial covenants` -> the certificate condition, 114 chars, silent.
- Em-dash carve-out ` - other than a Subsidiary that owns Material Intellectual Property or that guarantees the Notes` -> silent.

Doc 05 discloses that a condition *folded into a broader material span* is undetectable; it does not disclose that this extends to ~half of any boundary-free sentence.

### 7. MAJOR - line breaks and table rows are not segment boundaries
`inventory.ts:124`: `\n` is a boundary only when followed by an enumerator. A block of line-broken obligations is **one** segment. Verified: the 5-line reporting-covenant block below segments into exactly `1` segment of 335 non-ws chars.
```
Reporting Requirements
Annual audited consolidated financial statements within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year
Quarterly unaudited financial statements within 45 days after the end of each fiscal quarter
Notice of any Event of Default promptly upon a Responsible Officer obtaining knowledge thereof
Notice of any change in the Borrower jurisdiction of organization or fiscal year end
```
One item covering line 2 -> `INVENTORY_OK`, `0` segments, `uninventoriedValues: ["DAYS:45 days"]` (non-blocking per finding 2), `semanticallyComplete: true`, `[]`. Three reporting covenants and a deadline dropped. Extracted tables and bulleted baskets hit this every time; the two independent guards (single segment + no vocabulary) both fail open here.

### 8. MAJOR - granularity is model-controlled: one blanket item nullifies the entire layer
`inventory.ts:145` (`ACCOUNTING_SPAN`) + `:325`/`:344`. Coverage is span arithmetic over model-declared spans with model-declared materiality, with no upper bound on span size and no minimum item density.

- **Case E**: a single `CRITICAL` item whose excerpt is the *whole* 298-char region (two provisos, `$25,000,000`, `3.50 to 1.00`) -> `INVENTORY_OK`, `0` segments, `0` uninventoried values, `semanticallyComplete: true`, `[]`. Every accounting signal in the layer reads clean on an inventory that inventoried nothing.
- **Case F3 (the gap path)**: a genuine gap is correctly detected on `... shall not create any Lien, except Permitted Liens and Liens securing Capital Lease Obligations ...`; the gap call returns **one** item echoing the segment verbatim as `CRITICAL/OTHER` -> `segmentsAfter: 0`, `INVENTORY_OK`, `semanticallyComplete: true`, `[]`.

`prompt.ts:67-79` hands the model the uncovered segment text verbatim, so echoing it back is the cheapest possible response, and the *only* discriminator between the intended atomic inventory and a blanket echo is the model's self-declared `materiality` - for which `REVIEW_UNCERTAIN` is merely the wire-schema default (`wire-schema.ts:37`). The B2''-class fix (only CRITICAL/MATERIAL span counts) is defeated by a one-word change in the model's output. Nothing downstream re-checks span size, item count, or proposition density.

### 9. MINOR - the semantic-compiler cache key omits the accountability algorithm/prompt version
`lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/cache.ts:60-76`. The key hashes 13 fields; `SEMANTIC_ACCOUNTABILITY_ALGORITHM_VERSION` and `SEMANTIC_INVENTORY_PROMPT_VERSION` (`semantic-accountability/types.ts:33-34`) are among none of them - and `grep` confirms neither constant is referenced anywhere outside `semantic-accountability/`. `compile.ts:160-163` returns the cached `SemanticCompilationResult` **before** source-context resolution and Pass A run at all, so a result frozen under accountability `v1` (which had no `uninventoriedSegments` concept) is served verbatim after a bump to `v2`/`v3`. Blast radius today is one process (`compile.ts:41`, in-memory `defaultCache`) - but `cache.ts:6-16` explicitly designs this interface for a drop-in Postgres swap, at which point this becomes a durable stale-verdict channel.

### 10. MINOR - `frozenContentHash` is written but never verified
`inventory.ts:176-181` / `:204`. Nothing in the repo recomputes it. Contrast the sibling layer, which has `verifyFrozenInventoryUnchanged` (`semantic-coverage/freeze.ts:70-80`). The accountability "freeze" is a recorded digest, not an enforced one; no code path detects a `FrozenSemanticInventory` mutated between Pass A and Pass C.

## Claims I could **not** break (honest list)

- **Residual segments always surface once a gap is detected.** Gap call returning a non-covering item -> `INVENTORY_COVERAGE_GAP` + residual span. Gap call **throwing** -> `INVENTORY_COVERAGE_GAP` with the error text in the status reason, never `INVENTORY_OK`. Gap items marked `INFORMATIONAL`/`REVIEW_UNCERTAIN` -> gap stays open. All three verified live.
- **Materiality *downgrade* is fail-safe.** Relabelling an item to `INFORMATIONAL` removes its coverage and *creates* a gap (verified) - it can only hide text that was already invisible for one of reasons 1/4/6/7.
- **Status-string-alone.** The defense-in-depth checks are real: `reconciliation.ts:439` and `compile.ts:352` both key on `uninventoriedSegments.length > 0` independently of the status string. I found no input where a non-empty `uninventoriedSegments` failed to produce `SEMANTIC_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_GAP`.
- **Anti-hallucination gate.** An excerpt not present in any region is rejected and counted; an excerpt present only in another region locates *there*, so it cannot fabricate operative-region coverage. Duplicate ids are dropped and counted.
- **MONEY/PERCENT/RATIO in the operative region.** That gate works exactly as advertised, including under `REVIEW_UNCERTAIN`/`INFORMATIONAL` items.
- **`options.accountability === false`** is fail-safe downstream: `rollup.ts:22` turns a null accountability result into `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, not `SEMANTICALLY_COMPLETE`.

## Bottom line

The v2 layer is a genuine improvement on the *detected* path - once a gap is detected it cannot be talked away. The trust boundary fails on the *detection* path: eligibility to be a gap requires a closed vocabulary AND >=40 chars (or a bare-connective opener) AND <=50% span coverage AND a sentence/semicolon/enumerator boundary AND the OPERATIVE region - five conjunctive filters, each of which alone is sufficient to silence a material omission, and coverage itself is computed from model-declared spans with model-declared materiality. The pipeline should not be described as "can no longer silently omit material operative content"; on the evidence above the accurate description is "surfaces uncovered operative text that happens to match a fixed connective vocabulary, exceeds a length floor, and falls on a punctuation boundary." At minimum: findings 2 and 3 are one-line fixes (drop the kind and `regionId` filters, or state the residual as a first-class disclosed exclusion), and finding 8 needs a span-size/density check before `ACCOUNTING_SPAN` is trusted.
